archetypes.name: caller-completeness
archetypes.rationale: Plan names four SKILL.md callers and external-reviewers.md as the complete update surface, relying on the existing Edit-in-sync table in degraded-tools-gate.md as authoritative, without proving exhaustiveness against actual repo call sites.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan enumerates four SKILL.md files and `skills/shared/external-reviewers.md` as the complete set of callers requiring a `BOTH_DOWN`-aware update. Search the repository for every invocation of `degraded-tools-gate.sh` — in hooks, wrapper scripts, test fixtures, and any path not covered by the listed scope files — and compare against the plan's declared target list. Identify any call site the plan omits that either (a) parses the gate's KV output and branches on `DEGRADED`, or (b) surfaces the explanation block to the operator, since those sites need the same two-branch treatment to avoid presenting the old ask-always UX when only one tool is down. Also confirm whether the Edit-in-sync table in `scripts/degraded-tools-gate.md` itself is authoritative or whether it too needs a row update to reflect the new caller-side branching requirement. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: kv-parse-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds BOTH_DOWN as a new emitted KV but does not examine how each caller currently parses the gate output stream, leaving open whether the new key is reachable or silently dropped by the existing parse idiom.
archetypes.prompt_body: Each caller consumes `degraded-tools-gate.sh` stdout as a KV stream; the plan appends `BOTH_DOWN` after `CURSOR_STATE` in the emission order but does not show the parse idiom used in any of the five target files. Examine how `skills/design/SKILL.md`, `skills/implement/SKILL.md`, `skills/research/SKILL.md`, `skills/review/SKILL.md`, and `skills/shared/external-reviewers.md` currently instruct the orchestrator to parse the gate output — whether via `source`, `eval $(...)`, a named `parse_kv` helper, or line-by-line reads — and verify that inserting a new key after `CURSOR_STATE` is compatible with that idiom without silent truncation or an unset variable. Pay special attention to the plan's safety claim that an unset `BOTH_DOWN` defaults callers to old ask-always behavior, and confirm this holds for each parse form rather than causing a syntax error or treating the unset variable as an empty string that triggers the wrong branch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
